Evening Primrose Oil
Evening Primrose Oil is a natural oil that contains GLA, which is known to decrease ornithine carboxylase activity in breast tumors and acts as a hormone regulator.<SEP>Evening Primrose Oil is a source of Gamma Linolenic Acid (GLA) and is suggested for hormone regulation in breast cancer.

GLA
GLA (Gamma-Linolenic Acid) is a fatty acid found in Evening Primrose Oil that decreases ornithine carboxylase activity in breast tumors and is suggested to be taken at a dose of around 2g daily.

Paclitaxel
Paclitaxel is a chemotherapy drug that, when used in conjunction with GLA, can increase the response to Tamoxifen in breast cancer treatment.<SEP>Paclitaxel is a chemotherapy drug whose efficacy can be influenced by P-Glycoprotein and other drug resistance mechanisms.

Tamoxifen
Tamoxifen is a medication used to treat hormone receptor-positive breast cancer and is noted to be more effective when combined with GLA.<SEP>Tamoxifen is a medication used to treat hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

Grapeseed Extract OPCs
Grapeseed Extract OPCs are natural aromatase inhibitors that may play a role in breast cancer treatment.

Green Tea EGCG
EGCG (Epigallocatechin gallate) is a compound found in green tea known for its antioxidant and anti-cancer effects.<SEP>EGCG (Epigallocatechin gallate) is a powerful antioxidant found in green tea, known for its potential health benefits, including cancer prevention.<SEP>Green Tea EGCG is a compound that acts as a regulator of histone proteins and has implications in reducing drug resistance in cancer treatment.<SEP>Green Tea EGCG is a compound that reduces the risk of recurrence by 50% in post-operative stage I and II breast cancer and inhibits breast cancer cells via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor.<SEP>Green Tea EGCG is a natural compound that acts as a regulator of histone proteins and may help in reducing drug resistance in cancer treatment.

Indole-3 Carbinol 13C

DIM

Intravenous Artesunate

Lugol's Solution

Dr Max Gerson

Dickson Chemist

Melatonin
Melatonin is a hormone that benefits breast cancer patients, particularly those with ER+ breast cancer, by decreasing the production of estrogen receptors.<SEP>Melatonin is a hormone that can regulate hormone levels and may influence drug resistance in cancer treatment.<SEP>Melatonin is a hormone that regulates sleep-wake cycles and has been studied for its potential anti-cancer properties.

Pomegranates

Quercetin
Quercetin is a flavonoid found in many fruits and vegetables, known for its antioxidant properties and potential anti-cancer effects.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid that can act as a regulator of drug resistance proteins and is derived from various fruits and vegetables.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid that can regulate drug resistance proteins and has been noted for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory effects.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid that can regulate histone proteins and is noted for its potential to influence drug resistance mechanisms.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid that supports breast cancer treatment by activating receptors that make cancer cells more responsive to treatment.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid with antioxidant properties that may help in regulating cancer-related pathways in breast cancer treatment.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid with antioxidant properties that may help reduce inflammation and support immune function.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid with antioxidant properties that may play a role in cancer treatment and prevention.<SEP>Quercetin is a flavonoid with antioxidant properties, often studied for its potential health benefits including anti-cancer effects.

Resveratrol
Resveratrol is a compound found in Muscadine grapes that exhibits phytoestrogen properties and its safety varies by menopausal status.<SEP>Resveratrol is a phytoestrogen that blocks estrogen DNA adducts responsible for breast cancer, though its safety in post-menopausal ER+ women is still under research.<SEP>Resveratrol is a phytoestrogen that blocks estrogen DNA adducts, which are linked to breast cancer, and binds to estrogen receptors.<SEP>Resveratrol is a natural compound found in grapes and berries, known for its antioxidant properties and potential health benefits.<SEP>Resveratrol is a natural compound found in grapes and berries, known for its antioxidant properties and potential health benefits.

Equol

Flaxseeds

Breast Cancer
Breast cancer is a disease that can metastasize to other areas such as the brain and is monitored through MRI scans.<SEP>Pomegranates act as natural aromatase inhibitors and inhibit growth factors in breast cancer.<SEP>Breast cancer is a type of cancer that develops from breast tissue and is characterized by the production of aromatase and other genetic factors influencing its progression and treatment.<SEP>Breast cancer is a disease where malignant cells form in the tissues of the breast, and it can exhibit various biological behaviors, including brain metastases.<SEP>Breast cancer is a type of cancer that originates from breast tissue and can metastasize to other parts of the body.

The Blood Brain Barrier is a protective barrier consisting of capillary endothelial cells and membranes that restrict the passage of substances to the brain, including toxins and certain drugs.<SEP>The blood-brain barrier is a protective barrier that restricts substances from entering the brain, impacting treatment for conditions like cancer.

ABCG2, also known as BBRP or BCRP, is a protein that prevents drug resistance in breast cancer by limiting the penetration of certain drugs across the blood-brain barrier.<SEP>ABCG2, also known as BCRP, is a protein that plays a critical role in preventing drug resistance in breast cancer.

P-Glycoprotein (P-gp) is a protein that limits the bioavailability of orally taken drugs and contributes to drug resistance by pumping cytotoxins out of cells.<SEP>P-Glycoprotein is a membrane protein that pumps cytotoxins and certain drugs out of cells, impacting their bioavailability and contributing to drug resistance.

Histone protein acylation modulators are compounds that can impact drug resistance by affecting the function of certain proteins involved in multidrug resistance.<SEP>Histone protein acylation modulators are compounds that can influence the activity of MDRP-1, potentially reducing drug resistance in cancer treatments.

DMSO

Research Reference by Evelyn M. Brosnan
Evelyn M. Brosnan is a researcher focused on understanding brain metastasis patterns in breast cancer.

Breast Cancer Cells
Breast cancer cells are malignant cells that can adapt and change their metabolic pathways, allowing them to survive in adverse conditions, such as during chemotherapy.

Triple Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC)
Triple Negative Breast Cancer is a subtype of breast cancer that lacks three common receptors, making it more challenging to treat.

Cyclin D1
Cyclin D1 is a protein that regulates the cell cycle and is essential for the proliferation of HER2 positive breast cancer cells.

CDK4 and CDK6
Cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4 and CDK6) are enzymes that play a key role in cell cycle progression, particularly in HER2 positive breast cancer.

MiR-202-3p
MiR-202-3p is a microRNA that is downregulated in brain metastases of breast cancer, affecting cell migration and invasiveness.

MMP-1
MMP-1 (Matrix Metalloproteinase-1) is an enzyme that facilitates the migration of cancer cells and is overexpressed in brain metastases.

Heavy Metals
Heavy metals are environmental toxins that can upregulate MMP-1, potentially contributing to cancer progression.

Chelation
Chelation is a medical treatment that involves binding heavy metals to reduce their toxicity, which could be beneficial in cancer therapy.

COX-2
COX-2 is an enzyme associated with inflammation and is a target for regulating MMPs in cancer treatment.

Soy
Soy contains compounds that may influence cancer growth and has been studied for its potential protective effects.

Sulforaphanes
Sulforaphanes are compounds found in cruciferous vegetables that have shown promise in cancer prevention and treatment.

Vitamin D
Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin that is important for bone health and has been studied for its role in cancer biology.<SEP>Vitamin D is a nutrient that may have implications in cancer treatment, particularly in promoting cell cycle regulation.

Zeolite
Zeolite is a mineral that may have detoxifying properties and is being explored for its potential benefits in cancer therapy.

Bovine Cartilage
Bovine cartilage is a source of compounds that may support joint health and has been investigated for anti-cancer properties.

Research References
Research references include various studies and publications that provide insights into the mechanisms and treatments related to breast cancer.

YB-1
YB-1 is a compound that may refer to a specific chemical or biological entity, potentially studied for its health effects or applications.

Evelyn M. Brosnan
Evelyn M. Brosnan is a researcher involved in understanding brain metastasis in breast cancer and therapeutic strategies.

Carey K. Anders
Carey K. Anders is a researcher collaborating with Evelyn M. Brosnan on breast cancer research.

Glucose
Glucose is a simple sugar that is an important energy source in living organisms and plays a role in cancer metabolism.

Fatty Acids
Fatty acids are carboxylic acids with long aliphatic tails, which are important for various metabolic pathways, including those related to cancer.

Glutamine
Glutamine is an amino acid that is crucial for cellular metabolism and is often utilized by cancer cells.

Berberine
Berberine is a compound with potential therapeutic effects in cancer treatment and metabolic regulation.

Aspirin
Aspirin is a medication used to reduce pain and inflammation, and has been investigated for its role in cancer prevention.

Insulin
Insulin is a hormone that regulates glucose levels in the blood and has implications in cancer metabolism.

Blackseed Oil
Blackseed oil is derived from the seeds of the Nigella sativa plant and is known for its medicinal properties, including potential anti-cancer effects.<SEP>Blackseed oil is derived from the seeds of the Nigella sativa plant, known for its potential health benefits, including anti-cancer properties.

Omega 3 DHA
Omega 3 DHA is a fatty acid that is important for brain health and has been studied for its potential effects on cancer.

Cancer Feeding Pathways
Cancer Feeding Pathways refer to the various metabolic pathways that cancer cells use to derive nutrients necessary for growth and survival.<SEP>Cancer feeding pathways refer to the metabolic processes that cancer cells use to obtain nutrients and energy.

Lena Secky
Lena Secky is a researcher mentioned in the context of studies related to brain metastasis and cancer pathways.

Theresia Thalhammer
Theresia Thalhammer is another researcher involved in understanding cancer pathways and therapeutic strategies.

Atorvastatin
Atorvastatin is a medication typically used to lower cholesterol that has potential implications in cancer treatment.

Low GI Diet
A Low GI Diet consists of foods that have a low glycemic index, which may help manage insulin levels and has implications for cancer treatment.

DHEA
DHEA (Dehydroepiandrosterone) is a hormone that is sometimes studied for its effects on cancer, particularly hormone-sensitive cancers.

IV Vit C infusions
IV Vitamin C infusions are treatments that deliver high doses of vitamin C directly into the bloodstream and are explored for their potential anti-cancer effects.

Liposomal Ascorbate
Liposomal Ascorbate refers to a form of Vitamin C encapsulated in liposomes, enhancing its bioavailability and potential therapeutic effects in cancer.

Hydroxycitrate
Hydroxycitrate is a compound that may have implications in cancer treatment by influencing metabolic pathways.

DNA hyper-methylation
DNA hyper-methylation refers to a process that can silence tumor suppressor genes and is relevant in cancer biology.

E-Cadherin
E-Cadherin is a protein that helps cells stick together and is important in maintaining tissue architecture, often studied in cancer metastasis.

Insulin Like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
IGF-1 is a hormone that plays a role in growth and development and has implications in cancer cell proliferation.

NFkB
NFkB is a protein complex that controls transcription of DNA and is involved in cellular responses to stress, inflammation, and cancer progression.

P13K/Akt/mTOR
The P13K/Akt/mTOR pathway is a signaling pathway that regulates cell growth and metabolism, often implicated in cancer.

STAT-3
STAT-3 is a transcription factor that, when activated, can promote cancer cell survival and proliferation.

Survivin
Survivin is a protein that inhibits apoptosis and is often overexpressed in cancer cells, contributing to tumor survival.

TNF
TNF (Tumor Necrosis Factor) is a cytokine involved in systemic inflammation and has roles in cancer progression.

Grapeseed OPCs
Grapeseed OPCs (Oligomeric Proanthocyanidins) are antioxidants derived from grape seeds that may have health benefits, including potential anti-cancer effects.
